The attribute address of the character being drawn.
The next character number of the graphic being drawn.
The next attribute of the colour set being drawn.

Draws graphic A, nine characters in three rows of three (from the scenario's table at ($D038), nine character numbers a graphic, the characters from the set at $D03D), in colour set B (nine attributes a set, from ($D036)): one square of the map.
draw_block_at for thing A: thing_graphic then the drawing.

A = the graphic and B = the colour set of thing A (a map byte: terrain, object or creature), from its five-byte entry in the scenario's table at ($D032). Byte 0 picks the character set, from the scenario's table of sets at $D07A, when it is not the one in use ($D03C, address in $D03D). Bytes 3 and 4 are its animation: the frames left and the next frame.

The interrupt routine, every frame through the vector at $FFFF: interrupts off (DI) at its start, then on every second frame the main work ($A891), on every frame the information display's bars slide when bit 4 of $D0DF is set ($AB0E), and EI before RETI.

The work of every second frame, keeping the drawing state of the main program: every animated thing (170 five-byte entries in ($D032); a count of $FF is not animated) counts down and at 0 takes its next frame ($A936); the cursor blinks ($AA83); the flashing colour $FF53 takes the next value from the list at $B494. Then by the bits of $D0DF: bit 0 redraws the map window, bit 1 the information display's pictures and icons ($AAA5), bit 2 the first two pictures only ($AA9F), bit 3 the menu bar ($AAD4); with $5B42 set the message line flashes. Restoring the state, the instruction at $A914 reads block_colours instead of writing it back, so a block the main program is drawing when the interrupt comes takes the rest of its attributes from wherever the interrupt's own drawing left the pointer.
A byte nothing reads.
The thing whose animation count (its address in HL) has run out takes its next frame: graphic, colour set, count and next frame, four bytes from the scenario's frame table at ($D034).

Draws the map window, seven squares by seven from the top left square ($D0C8, row and column, wrapping at 36): each square's thing (map byte), looked up as thing_graphic does, the same steps written out again, except the cursor's square while the cursor is on ($D0D0), which shows the cursor (graphic and colours in $FF86, characters at $B646). A sound in progress ($C839) gets a step after each row.
map_address for the map window's top left square, $D0CC.
map_address for the cursor's square, $D0D3.
map_address for the selected creature's square, $5B55.
HL = the address in the map (36 by 36 bytes at ($D030)) of the square at row L, column H.
Turns the cursor on ($D0D0) for three calls and off for two, counting in $B45B.
Redraws the first two pictures of the information display (a first of $FF is skipped).
Redraws the eight pictures of the information display, from the list at $B45C (thing, row and column each; the first is the terrain), skipping empty ones after the first, then flashes its icons.
Colours each icon of the information display that is on ($D1A9-$D1AD: undead, flying, mount, fatal wound, invisible) with the flashing colour $FF53.

Redraws the menu's pictures ($5B0A of them from $B474), colours the bar on the choice ($C662) with the flashing colour and waits about 167,600 T-states (delay_50, 50 x 255 turns of an empty loop), inside the interrupt.
Draws B things from a list of three bytes each at HL (thing, row, column), skipping one equal to C (C is 0 after the first).
Moves each of the information display's five bars one pixel toward its value: the drawn length at $D1F6 on, the value at $D1FB on (at most $5F), filling or clearing one pixel line of the bar ($AC99).
Prints message A from the engine's own text ($CE00 messages, $CE57 words) in its own font ($9531), single height.
Prints message A of the scenario in single height, unless the computer is moving ($D063).
Prints message A of the scenario in double height.
Prints message A from the scenario's tables ($D00B messages, $D00D words) in the ROM's font ($3C00).

Prints message A of the tables at ($FFFB) and ($FFFD) from the start of the line ($5B1A). A message is a length byte then word numbers and control codes; a word is a length byte then characters. Codes: $FF a new line (two lines down in double height), $FE a colour (one byte, two in double height), $FD and $FC turn a gap after each word on and off ($B45A; bit 1 prints a space in it), $FB a position (row and column). $FA in a word is skipped.
After a word: the gap, when $B45A asks for one.
HL = entry B of the list at HL, whose entries start with their length (entry 1 is the first); B = its length.
Acts on control code A ($FB-$FF) at HL; B counts the bytes it uses.
Prints character A at row $5B15, column $5B16, if the column is below 32: single height ($AF91) or double ($AFE2), by bit 3 of $5B14.
HL = the screen address of pixel line E, character column D.
Draws one pixel line of a bar's outline (the two side lines) at line E, column D.
Draws the top of a bar's outline at line E, column D.
Inverts the inside of one pixel line of a bar at line E, column D.

Draws the outlines of the five bars, upward from pixel line $97 in columns $16, $18 ... $1E, each as tall as its most value ($D200 on: action points, stamina, constitution, combat, defence), no higher than line $39.
Plots the pixel at line $FF33, column $FF34: set, cleared or flipped as $FF32 is 0, 1 or 2; when $FF61 is not $FF its character cell takes that attribute.
Plots shape $FF5D (from shapes) at the map window's pixel $FF5B, $FF5C, every point inside the window (below $A8).
The shapes of a flying missile: offsets (line, column) ending with $7F.
A cross of five pixels.
A star of thirteen pixels.
Where missile_step writes in the tail.
Empties the missile's tail, $FF5F bytes at $FF65 ending with $FE.
Draws the missile at its new place ($FF3B, $FF3C), keeps that in the tail and wipes it at the oldest place in the tail.
Wipes the missile's tail place by place, with a sound step each.

Draws something flying from the selected creature ($5B55) to the cursor's square ($D0D3), a pixel line at a time ($B0C9, after $B045 has set the line up) from the middle of the map window ($53, $53), $FF5E pixels a frame. Leaving the window moves the view seven squares that way and redraws the map. Every 24 pixels the square under it is checked against the target, and on reaching it the tail is wiped and the hit drawn.
Draws the hit on square E, D: the burst, things $53 to $55 from the characters at $BE3C, at the square's place in the window, with sound 8.
The missile has left the map window at the bottom: the window moves seven rows down the map (wrapping at 36) and the missile to its top line; $FF64 says the view moved.
The missile has left the window at the top: the window moves seven rows up and the missile to its bottom line ($A7).
The missile has left the window at the right: the window moves seven columns right and the missile to its left edge.
The missile has left the window at the left: the window moves seven columns left and the missile to its right edge ($A7).
The screen address of each of the 24 character rows.

Prints character A of the font at ($5B0E) at row $5B15, column $5B16 in attribute $5B17: as it is when bit 0 of $5B14 is set (the engine's own font), otherwise in bold (each line ored with itself moved right by a pixel).
Prints character A in double height and bold at rows $5B15 and $5B15 + 1, column $5B16: the top half in attribute $5B17, the bottom in $5B18.

Sets up a line from square $FF3B to square $FF3D on the wrapping map, the shorter way round each axis: the row and column steps ($FF3F, $FF40: 1 or $FF) and differences ($FF43, $FF44); the longer difference in $FF46 with the step along it alone in $FF41 or $FF42, the shorter in $FF45; the running error ($FF47) at half the longer; the length so far ($FF48) at 0.
line_step on pixel positions in the map window, which do not wrap.

Moves the point $FF3B, $FF3C one step along the line: a diagonal step when the error runs out (the length $FF48 goes up by 3), otherwise a step along the longer axis (the length goes up by 2). On the map ($FF35 = 0) the row and column wrap from 0 to 35.
A row or column of $FF becomes 35 ($23) and one of 36 becomes 0.

After the selected creature has moved or acted: works out what it sees ($B1A6; from under cover, bit 2 of its terrain's flags at $D38E, it sees less, unless it flies), puts it back on the map, reloads the computer's creature if new enemies were noted ($D187), and for a creature that may be engaged ($5B29) sets or clears its engaged bit (bit 4 of byte 4 of its record) as an enemy stands next to it at its height ($5B3F), unless bit 3 of that byte holds it.

Works out what can be seen from square HL ($FF88) at the selected creature's height. The reach is $13 half squares on the ground and $17 in the air, nine and eleven squares in a straight line, as the manual says. Every entry of the object table loses its seen mark (bit 6 of byte 1); the viewer has it. Every entry on a square within reach (by the distance's rule, in $FF4F) that is not riding is checked by a line traced over the ground ($B416), with the flags of the terrain it stands on ($FF4A, $FF4C), then see_square. Counts the enemies in view on the ground and in the air ($5B40, $5B41) as it goes.

Decides, for every entry from $5B1F on that stands on square $FF4D and has no seen mark yet, whether it is seen ($B2E8), and shows on the map the creature seen at the viewer's height, or else one at the other height, or else the heaviest object seen there.

Whether the entry at IX is seen. An invisible creature (bit 3 of byte 4 of its record) that is not the player's is not, unless the magic eye is open ($8A89). At another height than the viewer's, it is not when the viewer is under cover ($FF4B), or a creature on the ground is under cover ($FF4C). On the ground, a creature in the air is seen; otherwise one next to it ($FF4F below 4) or one the line reaches. In the air, a flying creature is seen; an object on terrain that hides from above ($FF4A) is not; otherwise one next to it or one under open sky. A seen entry is marked shown (bit 7 of byte 1): an object goes on the computer's list of objects seen ($D148, up to 24) and the heaviest object on the square ($5B2C, weight in $5B2E) is kept; an enemy creature loses its invisibility, is counted and noted, and so is a rider it carries.
Counts an enemy in view at height $D18F ($5B40 on the ground, $5B41 in the air), has the computer note it while it moves ($9C8C), and sets $5B3F when it stands next to the viewer at the same height.
A way into trace_line with flag $20 that nothing calls.
A way into trace_line with flag $40 that nothing calls.
trace_line with terrain flag $10, which blocks sight in the air.
trace_line with terrain flag $01, which blocks sight on the ground.

Follows the line from square $FF88 to square $FF4D over the map: Z set (and $FF49 0) when no square on the way has the flag $5B2B among its terrain's flags (the table at $D38E); Z clear and $FF49 = 1 when one blocks it.
The gap after each word of a message: 0 none, 1 a column skipped, with bit 1 a space printed.
Counts the calls to blink_cursor left before the cursor changes.
The information display's eight pictures, three bytes each (thing, row, column): the terrain, the creature, then six objects in two columns.
The pictures beside the ten lines of a list (choose_from_list), three bytes each, in two columns at rows 3, 7, 11, 15 and 19.
The next colour of flash_colours.
The attributes the flashing things cycle through, ending with $FF: bright red, magenta, green, cyan, yellow and back.
The steps to the eight squares around a square, row then column, clockwise from the one above.
The chance numbers spread_magic uses for gooey blob dying back, by strength.
The chance numbers spread_magic uses for magic fire dying back, by strength.
The base mana cost of each of the 45 spells; a cast costs the base times the spell's level plus one.

Moves the selected creature to square $FF8A: the old square shows again what lay under it ($FF90), the new one's map byte (at $FF8C) is kept and replaced by the creature. Its terrain becomes $FF91; the step's cost ($FF8E) comes off its action points and half of it off its stamina. What it carries, and its rider or mount, move with it; then update_view.
Puts the entry at IX on square L (row), H (column), keeping the top two bits of byte 1.
Moves to square HL, with terrain $FF91, every entry that the selected creature ($5B4F) or its rider ($5B44) carries.
creature_record for the creature number in byte 5 of the entry at IX.
IY = the record of creature A: five bytes each at $5EC0 (action points, stamina, constitution, potion, flags).
type_record for the type in byte 2 of the entry at IX.
IY = the record of creature type A: for $90 up, twelve bytes each from ($D003) in the scenario; for a wizard ($8C-$8F), the 23 bytes from byte 47 of the player's wizard record.
Keeps the selected creature's square, terrain, action points and stamina ($5B30-$5B34).
Copies missile style A (eight bytes each from missile_styles) into $FF5D on: shape, pixels a frame, tail length, reach, attribute, combat and magic; and plays its sound (the eighth byte).
The missile styles: 0 a dragon's flame (reach $0C, combat 35), 1 an arrow (reach $10, combat 15), 2 a magic arrow (reach $16, combat 30, magic), 3 a thrown object, then the spells' bolts.
Character set 0 of the map's graphics (the scenario's table at $D07A points to it), which also holds the cursor: here its first 128 characters.
Character set 0 from its character 128 to the end, $BE3B.
Character set 1 of the map's graphics, 245 characters, with the burst a hit shows ($AEC2): here its first 56 and a half.
Character set 1 from $C000, the middle of its character 56, to the middle of character 184.
The rest of character set 1, to its last character, 244, at $C5DC.
1 when the last load failed or was broken off with SPACE, 0 when it worked. After a save it is always 1: tape_transfer sets it and only a load that works clears it.
Loads DE bytes with flag byte B into IX from tape through the ROM's LD-BYTES, entered at $0562 with a white border; tape_error says how it went.
Saves DE bytes from IX with flag byte B through the ROM's SA-BYTES ($04C6).
The common part: A is 1 to load, 0 to save.

Calls LD-BYTES past its own set-up, with tape_check as its return.

1 while loading, 0 while saving.
The twelve characters of the file name the player typed, the last three its extension.
The $FF after the file name.
Puts the three characters at HL into the file name's extension.
The extension of a wizard file.
The extension of a saved game.
The extension of a scenario.
The name of the designer's file.
The option chosen on the last menu.
A value the file panels keep (used by the panels at $CC45 and by the designer).
A second value the file panels keep.
Saves the file name as the game's own header (twelve bytes, flag $64) and waits.

Reads the game's headers from tape (twelve bytes, flag $64, into found_name) until one matches the file name, showing each name found at row $16, column $0B with SEARCHING: and LOADING:. Z set when SPACE was held. Only the first character is compared (B is loaded with 12 but nothing counts it down), so the first file whose name starts with the same letter or digit is taken, whatever its extension.
The name in the last header read from tape.
SAVE WIZARD: saves the chosen wizard's 70-byte record ($CEA4 + 70 x (choice + 1)) with a header named with the extension WIZ.
LOAD WIZARD: finds the file and loads 70 bytes into the chosen wizard's record.
LOAD SCENARIO: asks for the file name, finds the file (extension GAM) and loads $2FFD bytes at $D003. On success the panel starts again ($CC39); on failure it returns.
LOAD DESIGNER: finds the file DESIGNER. and loads $0E45 bytes at $D3DC, then starts the designer there.
Saves the game: asks for the file name and saves a header (extension SVG), the object table and the creature records ($0514 bytes from $5B5A) and everything from $CEEA to the top of memory.
LOAD SAVED GAME: finds the file and loads its two blocks back, then goes into the game's turn loop; a failure goes back to the panel.

The menu at the end of each game turn (the scenario's message $E8): CONTINUE goes back to the turn loop; ABANDON forgets the scenario ($D03F) and goes back to the file panel; SAVE GAME saves it, but in a game against the computer only five times ($D068 counts; the menu comes back after the fifth).

Makes a wizard at random in record $5B04 for a player with none: 80 mana, level 0, each of the 45 spells at a random level from 0 to 2, the standard figures and the name WIZARD followed by the player's number.
The figures of a wizard made at random (twelve bytes, laid out as a creature type) and its name.
Draws a frame in the game's own font from row $5B00, column $5B01 to row $5B02, column $5B03 (HL and DE): corners, top and bottom edges, sides.

Classifies a step of the selected creature to square HL into $FF8F, keeping the square ($FF8A), its map address ($FF8C) and terrain ($FF91): 4 an enemy there at the creature's height (3 when the creature has a partner on its square and did not just dismount); otherwise 7 just dismounted in the air; 0 a square it cannot enter; 1 too few action points for the step's cost ($FF8E, half as much again on a diagonal, $FF92); 2 too little stamina (half the cost); 5 free; 6 free but the creature is engaged. The cost is the terrain's (byte 0 of its record; $FF cannot be entered), 4 for a ghost ($A5) or a flying creature, or 4 when the creature's type flags (bits 4-6 of byte 11) match the terrain's (bits 0-2 of byte 4): swimmers in water, for example. In the air a terrain with bit 3 of byte 4 set cannot be entered.
Runs a file panel's menu: up and down move the bar over the $5B0A options (menu_choice, wrapping round), with the key repeat; fire chooses, with sound 0.
Draws the scenario's file panel: the title (message $E6) with the number of the scenario loaded ($D03F, or message $E7 for none) in one frame and the four wizards in another.

Lists the four wizards from row $11 upward, two rows each: a slot whose record has a level (byte 1) shows the name, copied into the scenario's table of names and printed as message $8C + the player, and the level; an empty one shows message $E7.
Clears two rows of fourteen characters from the start of the line ($5B1A) in attribute A.

The scenario's file panel, with the interrupts in mode 1 and the stack at $606E: PLAY GAME, LOAD SCENARIO, LOAD DESIGNER, LOAD WIZARD, LOAD SAVED GAME and SAVE WIZARD, each through file_actions; the option chosen is kept in panel_value_1 while it runs.
Jumps to the routine for file panel option A.
The routines of the six options of the file panel.

LOAD WIZARD: chooses one of the four slots (the one last used, panel_value_2, first), asks for the file name and loads it; a failed load leaves the slot empty (byte 1 cleared). The list is drawn again.

SAVE WIZARD: chooses a slot and, when it holds a wizard, saves it under a name made of the first word of its name, at most seven letters ($FA counts as a space), followed by its level as a digit (10 and up as A, B ...).

FILE NAME: reads up to eight characters into file_name through the ROM's KEY-SCAN, using the key table: ENTER ends it, the 0 key rubs out the last character, symbol shift does nothing; each key gives sound 0 and waits until it is let go.
Prints the eight characters of the file name.
Prints B characters from DE in double height from the start of the line, in attribute $46 ($FA as a space).
The character of each key, by the number the ROM's KEY-SCAN gives it (0 for symbol shift and ENTER; caps shift, 39, is left out).
The engine's own six messages, which draw the information display's frame, icons and bars in the game's font.
The engine's own fourteen words: rows of characters of the game's font, with colours.
